content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early 30-day forecasts — adjust upward by 1–2% for initial periods.
- When sentiment is negative (avg < -0.4), forecasts tend to be too low; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5 units to compensate for bearish bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model overreacts and forecasts overshoot — cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons — if forecast is >+1.5% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 0.3–0.7 units.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > -0.2) after 3–5 days of negative sentiment, model lags in catching upward momentum — add 0.3–0.8 units to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme lows (below 38.5) unless confirmed by sentiment or event — if sentiment is neutral or positive, avoid under 40.0.
